acceptance.output_evidence:
STATED FOR 3.0.0_SA_CVO, NOT SELF-GRADED.

(1) WHERE 'PROGRAMMATIC BY DEFAULT, REVIEW THE EXCEPTION' BECOMES 'REVIEW EVERYTHING'.
At three places, and the first is the one that will actually happen.

  (i) A MONEY COLUMN WITH NO ISO CODE ANYWHERE. Almost no advisor writes `Market Value (USD)`;
      they write `Market Value`, and the currency is a thing everyone at the firm knows. This
      parser therefore reads UNDECLARED on a real workbook's money column, makes NO currency
      claim, and -- by the design this cell chose -- leaves round 1's unit token in place and
      says nothing. That is NOT review-everything; it is the opposite, and it is the honest
      boundary of the control: the four controls only speak when the document speaks. The count
      is printed as `undeclared_money_rows` in the currency reconcile precisely so nobody reads
      silence as confirmation. IF a future cell decides an undeclared money column must also
      quarantine, EVERY workbook quarantines on day one and the exception becomes the rule.
      That decision is not this cell's and the number to make it on is already being printed.

  (ii) ANY WORKBOOK FORMATTED AS CURRENCY IN EXCEL. Excel's own currency formats carry a symbol
      and a LOCALE (`[$$-409]`), never an ISO code. This cell reads that coordinate and
      correctly refuses to establish from it -- so a workbook that a human would call
      unambiguously USD quarantines on every money row. On a book of 200 client workbooks that
      is 200 reviews, and the reviewer's answer will be 'yes, USD' 200 times. The remedy is a
      FIRM-LEVEL declaration (this firm reports in USD) that is an INPUT to the parser rather
      than an inference by it -- which preserves the law, because the currency would then be
      established by a document Opal controls instead of guessed from a glyph.

  (iii) SUBTOTALLED WORKBOOKS. Grouped-with-subtotals is a common shape, and every one now
      quarantines with SUBTOTAL_ROW_PRESENT. The finding is correct and the reviewer's action is
      real (confirm which rows the subtotal covers), but it is UNCERTAIN severity on a shape
      that may be the majority of real specimens. If it is, the severity is the thing to revisit,
      not the detector.

(2) WHICH CURRENCY SIGNALS THE SPECIMENS COULD NOT REPRESENT.
  * A currency declared ONCE, at workbook or sheet level -- a title cell, a header, a footer, a
    note row, or a cover sheet -- and nowhere near the value. This is DECLARED as a blind spot
    in settings.json, and it is probably the single most common way a real workbook says CAD.
  * A MIXED-CURRENCY workbook: a Currency column whose value differs per row, or two money
    columns in different currencies. The machinery is per-row and would handle it, but no
    specimen exercises it, so that is an untested path and not a proven one.
  * An xlsx numFmt carrying a genuine ISO token (`[$CAD]`) -- the ESTABLISHING branch of the
    number-format coordinate is written and is exercised only by its refusing sibling here.
  * A currency in the filename, in the mail body, or stated by the advisor in a covering
    sentence. The first is deliberately not read; the last two are not visible to a parser at all
    and are the shape most likely to be the real answer in practice.
  * Accounting formats with parentheses AND a symbol, right-aligned symbols, non-breaking spaces
    between symbol and number, and every locale decimal convention (1.234,56). The specimens are
    ASCII and comma-grouped.

(3) WHAT A QUARANTINED SPECIMEN LOOKS LIKE TO THE ADVISOR WHO FORWARDED IT.
Today: a StatusEnvelope with state NEEDS_CORRECTION, public_reason_code PARSE_NEEDS_CORRECTION,
and one action, CORRECT. The findings carry a source cell (`holdings_non_usd.csv!C2`) and prose
naming what was established and where. THE HONEST ASSESSMENT: that is good for an operator and
thin for an advisor. The advisor sent a file and gets back 'needs correction' plus cell
references -- and nothing in this cell puts the finding in front of them, because the project
notifies nobody by bound 2 and the parser is wired to no route. So a quarantine is CURRENTLY a
state that exists correctly and reaches no one, and the person who has to act on it is an Opal
operator reading the envelope, not the advisor. Whether the advisor should see 'row 2 of your
file states CAD and we support USD -- resend in USD or confirm a conversion rate' is a product
decision this cell deliberately does not make.

AND THE BOUNDARY ON ALL OF THE ABOVE: every specimen here is synthetic and adversarial by
construction, and parse.py is packaged by 0 of 214 functions, so none of this has ever met a
real advisor's workbook in a real runtime. The controls are proven; the ENCOUNTER is not.
